Hyundai Motor GroupHyundai Motor Group is turning to a "data flywheel" and vision-language-action (VLA) models to close the gap in its self-driving development, saying it expects to surpass the volume of data accumulated by rivals including Tesla by 2033.Hyundai Motor (005380.KS) Group laid out the strategy at a self-driving media day held on the 11th at the headquarters of 42dot in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. Attendees included key figures in the group's autonomous driving effort: Park Min-woo, president and head of Hyundai Motor and Kia's AVP Division and chief executive of 42dot; Kwon Jung-hyun, executive vice president and head of the two automakers' autonomous driving development center and lead of 42dot's AD Division; Chung Sung-kyun, lead of 42dot's Atria Group; and Lee Hee-seok, lead of 42dot's Tryon Group. "Hyundai Motor Group will build differentiated competitiveness in autonomous driving by combining the ability to develop software and AI in-house with the ability to deliver that technology in vehicles and customer experiences on a global scale," Park said.The core concept the group presented was the data flywheel — a self-reinforcing cycle in which data collected from vehicles is used to train and validate artificial intelligence models, and the improved models are then deployed back to vehicles to gather fresh data. "Competition in autonomous driving is no longer a contest over specific features," Park said. "What determines a company's competitiveness is how much data it can secure, how quickly it can learn from that data, and how fast it can reflect the results in actual products and services."Hyundai Motor Group sells more than 7 million vehicles a year in about 190 countries, an installed base that would allow it to gather real-world driving data quickly once self-driving systems begin shipping. "Once mass production of autonomous driving systems begins in earnest, we will surpass the volume of data accumulated by our competitors within five years," Chung said.From second from left: Kwon Jung-hyun, head of Hyundai Motor and Kia's autonomous driving development center (executive vice president) and AD division lead at 42dot; Park Min-woo, head of Hyundai Motor and Kia's AVP division (president) and chief executive of 42dot; Chung Sung-kyun, Atria Group lead at 42dot; and Lee Hee-seok, Trion Group lead at 42dot, answer questions at an "Autonomous Driving Media Day" held on Nov. 11 at 42dot's headquarters in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. Hyundai Motor GroupThe group plans to apply Level 2+ autonomous driving functions based on Nvidia solutions to mass-produced vehicles in the first half of 2028, and to launch vehicles with Level 2++ features in the second half of that year. On the group's own timeline, that puts it ahead of rivals on data volume by 2033. Level 2+ refers to driver-assistance technology that allows hands-off driving under a driver's supervision in specific conditions such as highways, while Level 2++ extends that capability to ordinary roads and urban areas.Hyundai Motor Group will expand the technology in stages, including mass production in the second half of 2029 of Level 2++ systems built on its own autonomous driving platform, Atria AI, rather than Nvidia solutions. "By 2027, we will implement a range of functions — driving, parking and active safety — at a high level of completeness," Kwon said. "After that, think of 2028 as the period for gathering large amounts of data on edge cases, or exceptional driving situations, to build a product that is genuinely safe, and 2029 as the period for preparing safety certification not only in South Korea but also in North America and Europe."The group also released, for the first time, video of a software-defined vehicle (SDV) testbed car equipped with Atria AI driving through complex urban streets at a Level 2++ standard. The testbed vehicle, based on the Ioniq 6, carries eight cameras and one radar unit. Working with the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the group plans to deploy autonomous SDV pace cars in Gwangju, South Jeolla Province, from the end of this year to test the performance and stability of the technology on domestic roads.Ioniq-based autonomous driving test and data collection vehicles are on display at the "Vehicle Workshop" at 42dot's headquarters in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, on Nov. 11.
